title: Citizens’ assemblies are being institutionalized as a way to bring time, information, civic lottery, and deliberation into democratic decisions beyond elections
source_unit: newDemocracy Foundation, Democracy Beyond Elections: A Handbook on Citizens' Assemblies, second edition, produced with UNDP and UN Democracy Fund support
geography: Global deliberative-democracy practice, with examples of citizens’ assemblies addressing climate change, constitutional reform, and other major public decisions

observations.period: 2026 second edition; global citizens’ assembly practice

denominator.unit: handbook and growing global Democracy R&D practice network

institutional_model.value: Citizens’ assemblies use civic lottery to select everyday people and give them time, information, and opportunity to deliberate together

decision_scope.value: The handbook describes use for high-stakes challenges including climate change and constitutional reform

democratic_goal.value: The model aims to support more informed, substantive, representative, and trusted democratic decisions

observations.method: Practical handbook synthesizing experience and lessons from citizens’ assemblies and the Democracy R&D network, produced by newDemocracy with UNDP and UN Democracy Fund support.
observations.uncertainty: A handbook and practice network are not a representative evaluation, causal test, or proof that assemblies improve policy outcomes, legitimacy, or equality in every context.
observations.subgroup: Randomly selected citizens, elected officials, public servants, facilitators, experts, civil society, communities affected by policy, and people traditionally excluded from formal decision-making.
observations.counterinterpretation: Civic lottery and deliberation can broaden voice, while recruitment, support, facilitation, agenda-setting, and unequal ability to participate can still shape whose knowledge enters the room.

time_condition.value: Deliberation depends on giving participants sufficient time to learn, listen, weigh evidence, and think together

information_condition.value: Access to balanced information and structured learning is treated as part of meaningful participation

agency_condition.value: The model seeks to give ordinary people a substantive role in considering and recommending responses to major public questions

observations.method: Handbook guidance on commissioning, designing, operating, and learning from citizens’ assemblies.
observations.uncertainty: Design principles do not establish participant comprehension, deliberative equality, recommendation quality, or whether decision-makers act on recommendations.
observations.subgroup: Participants with different education, income, language, disability, age, racial, geographic, and political backgrounds; facilitators; experts; and decision-makers.
observations.counterinterpretation: More time and information can improve deliberation, but participation can impose unpaid care, work, travel, accessibility, and emotional costs that filter who can serve.

trust_route.value: Citizens’ assemblies are presented as a way to support trusted decisions through representative deliberation rather than electoral choice alone

representation_route.value: Civic lottery is used to approximate a cross-section of the public in a deliberative mini-public

beyond_elections.value: The model expands democratic participation beyond periodic voting toward sustained consideration of policy questions

observations.method: Handbook synthesis of deliberative-democracy practice and institutional design.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived trust, representativeness, and legitimacy require context-specific measurement; a mini-public cannot substitute for broad public accountability, elections, or organized civil society.
observations.subgroup: Citizens, elected officials, parties, civil-society organizations, public servants, media, and groups with low trust or weak access to traditional political channels.
observations.counterinterpretation: Assemblies can complement representative democracy, but they can also be used symbolically, delay decisions, or shift responsibility to selected citizens without transferring real authority.

commissioning_route.value: The handbook focuses on how political leaders, public officials, and practitioners can commission, design, and operate assemblies

follow_through.value: The democratic value of an assembly depends on how recommendations connect to policymaking, public explanation, and institutional response

learning_route.value: The handbook shares practical lessons and case experience to support future deliberative practice

observations.method: Practice-oriented guidance drawing on global cases and a deliberative-democracy practitioner network.
observations.uncertainty: The public description does not establish a common implementation standard, enforcement mechanism, or outcome benchmark across assemblies.
observations.subgroup: Decision-makers, public administrations, facilitators, experts, participants, civil-society observers, media, and communities affected by recommendations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutionalizing assemblies can create a durable feedback channel, but bureaucratic adoption can turn deliberation into a procedural box-checking exercise if agenda, authority, and feedback remain controlled elsewhere.

related_sources.claim: EU Joint Research Centre community page describes the handbook as a guide for commissioning, designing, and operating citizens’ assemblies.

boundary: This record adds a democratic-institution signal linking civic lottery, time, information, deliberation, representation, agency, trust, policymaking, and institutional follow-through. It is a practical handbook and practice synthesis, not a representative public-opinion dataset, respondent-level ingestion, causal evaluation, or proof that citizens’ assemblies produce trusted or equitable outcomes in every setting.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official newDemocracy publication page reviewed for second-edition status, UNDP and UN Democracy Fund partnership, civic-lottery model, time/information conditions, climate and constitutional applications, representation/trust objective, and implementation guidance.
